types.Question: A genuine unknown that needs a ruling or decision before play can rely on it.
types.Thread: A narrative hook that's been introduced but not yet picked back up — nobody's blocked on it, it's just dangling.
types.Consequence: Something that has already happened whose fallout hasn't played out yet.

items.title: Which ship, exactly, was pirated from Scarem Montem?
items.context: While planning Wilhelm's 1224 return trip, the table half-remembered that one of the covenant's own ships was originally taken from Scarem Montem — but didn't pin down which one, or the circumstances.
items.raised_event: An old wrinkle resurfaces: one of the covenant's ships was pirated from Scarem Montem
items.resolution: Confirmed by the GM (2026-07-13): it's the Hound of Cassel — a Tremere-crewed Scarem Montem vessel, raided by Valdemar's crew in Summer 1221 ("Summer piracy").

items.title: What are the remaining ~20 prize pawns actually being spent on?
items.context: Only the first three picks (Mont-Saint-Michel tide pools, the Terram summa "De Lapii", Subtle Knives) are locked in. The GM's notes on the rest of the prize list were incomplete as of session 7 and still need a second pass.
items.raised_event: Looking to 1224: back to Scarem Montem, and a still-unfinished prize list

items.title: Who staffs which vis-harvesting season now that the resource list has grown?
items.context: Explicitly deferred at the table as "too much to think about right now." With a much larger prize/resource footprint post-Tribunal, the covenant needs a real delegation plan.
items.raised_event: Looking to 1224: back to Scarem Montem, and a still-unfinished prize list

items.title: What was Valerian's interrogation of Wilhelm actually concurrent with?
items.context: The event's date field still reads "during Dagmar's dimicatio semifinal," but the GM-corrected Day-4 chronological order now places it after both the dimicatio semifinal AND the dimicatio final. Either the concurrency detail needs updating, or the event's position does.
items.raised_event: Valerian interrogates Wilhelm about the Brabant/Church conspiracy

items.title: Is "Siege of Notatus" the real name of the 7th-place honor, or a mis-transcription?
items.context: Confirmed only against the tribunal workbook's prize-rank table (which itself may have been typed from the same unclear audio) — not independently verified against the session recording.
items.raised_event: Tribunal final standings: Sjórseiðr takes first overall, Confluensis takes the "Siege of Shame"

items.title: Is the "Adamant" the same ship as the fleet's fifth hull, commissioned at Bergen and given to Valerian?
items.context: "Sorting through Solving's letters..." (Spring 1220) has a shipwright's letter announcing the fifth and final ship of the fleet is complete at Bergen. "Valerian's Arrival" (Spring 1222) has Valerian "given the newly purchased fifth ship and skeleton crew." The name "Adamant" only appears later.
items.raised_event: Valerian's Arrival
items.resolution: Confirmed by the GM (2026-07-13): the Adamant is the fifth hull commissioned at Bergen.

items.title: What happened to the Hound of Cassel — the ship captured in the Summer 1221 piracy raid?
items.context: Raided by Valdemar's crew from what's now confirmed to be a Tremere-crewed Scarem Montem vessel; yielded three magically-sealed chests and the letter that led to discovering the imprisoned Valerian de Castellane. The party debated "keep as prize or sink," leaning toward selling at a shadow port — but no event ever confirmed what actually happened to it.
items.raised_event: Summer piracy
items.resolution: Per the GM (2026-07-13): Wilhelm will effectively gain the Hound of Cassel, either to keep as his own ship or to use as a trade chip — and since it's the very ship pirated from Scarem Montem (see q001), that trade chip is literally their own hull back.

items.title: Which specific ship does Stijntje/Dustin actually sail on for the Ireland leg?
items.context: The Fall 1223 travel plan names only the Brineborn (Éogan, Wilhelm, Hilda, one assistant) and the Adamant (Valerian, Dietrich, one assistant); a later addendum has Dustin opting in and bringing Stijntje, without re-stating which hull they board.
items.raised_event: Ireland travel plan finalized: Dublin, the coast, and wintering near Carrick
items.resolution: Confirmed by the GM (2026-07-13): the Scholar's Wake — Dustin and Stijntje sail their own ship, traveling alongside the Brineborn.

items.title: Did Captain Absalom actually captain the Maelstrom's Maw, or a separate ship trading with it?
items.context: "Trade / Trading vis / A Hamlet to Work In" (Summer 1221) has Kor sending "Captain Absalom off to trade with the Maelstrom's Maw" — grammatically ambiguous between two different ships, or Absalom captaining the Maelstrom's Maw itself.
items.raised_event: Trade / Trading vis / A Hamlet to Work In

items.title: Did Garrat Coffin transfer from the Brineborn to Veðrdreki at some point, or is the chronicle's older note wrong?
items.context: "Traveling to the Tribunal" and "Up the Sarthe to Le Mans" (Summer 1223) both describe Garrett/Garrat Coffin and Drest as "from the Brineborn." The current standing-crew roster instead places Garrat Coffin on Veðrdreki (the Storm Dragon), with only Drest remaining on the Brineborn.
items.raised_in: Cross-referenced against the GM's crew roster (2026-07-13)
items.raised_event: Traveling to the Tribunal
items.resolution: Confirmed by the GM (2026-07-13): he transferred.

items.title: What are Wilhelm's remaining Virtues and Flaws?
items.context: Sheet as introduced only firmly lists Minor Magical Focus; two further Virtues (and a full Flaws list) are still marked TBD.
items.raised_event: Wilhelm Stienauer ex Bonisagus arrives

items.title: The ship-for-book swap with Scarem Montem hasn't been pitched yet.
items.context: Two framings were floated: rough justice ("fair's fair," they took the book, the covenant already has the ship) or a literal bargaining chip. Now confirmed the Hound of Cassel IS the ship pirated from Scarem Montem, and Wilhelm is set to gain it — does the party actually offer their own hull back in exchange for the thesis when he returns in 1224?
items.raised_event: An old wrinkle resurfaces: one of the covenant's ships was pirated from Scarem Montem

items.title: Wilhelm's thesis still needs a maritime hedge-tradition example.
items.context: Dowsing-for-fresh-water is confirmed; open-ocean current-finding or storm prediction is the thesis's weakest citation and the whole reason for the Ireland trip.
items.raised_event: Wilhelm pitches Éogan on hedge-magic sea/weather traditions for the thesis

items.title: Éogan hasn't told the rest of the covenant about Bridget's Lotharingian pitch.
items.context: Bridget of Scarem Montem (House Tremere) offered to hold Éogan's Tourney winnings outside Normandy's recall jurisdiction, as part of a broader Lotharingian-secession pitch. As of the Tribunal, Éogan had kept this to himself.
items.raised_event: Bridget of Scarem Montem's Lotharingian pitch

items.title: Dagmar has never surfaced what he saw of Valerian's contraband trade.
items.context: Dagmar caught Valerian trading Rhine-Tribunal-contraband books with an unidentified Montverte magus and quietly walked away without confronting him or reporting it. A second, untrusted axis through the Montverte relationship that's never been addressed.
items.raised_event: Dagmar spots Valerian trading contraband

items.title: Hervé of Turris Vigilans's mutual-defense pact has never been formally invoked.
items.context: Valdemar accepted the blue sash (the signal of accord) but never wore it publicly. His joust "win" over Hervé was unintentional (Rosie's squeal spooked Hervé's mount) — does Hervé believe that, and does the pact still stand?
items.raised_event: Hervé of Turris Vigilans's mutual-defense pact for Valdemar

items.title: Raoul of Oleron's original light-handed-liege pitch to Éogan was never formally closed out.
items.context: Raoul's pitch: a top-three finish would trigger vassalage pressure from somebody, so pick the gentlest liege now. The party never took him up on it, but the two covenants ended up on excellent terms anyway after the Tribunal. Does Raoul ever raise it again?
items.raised_event: Raoul of Oleron's light-handed liege offer to Éogan

items.title: Llewellyn's time-crystal offer to Dagmar is still on the table.
items.context: A quartz crystal "resonant with the platonic ideal of time" — effectively a magical atomic clock for detecting time dilation in regiones, directly complementing Dagmar's commission with Paulus. Price: accompany Llewellyn into a regio of Dagmar's choosing. Dagmar expressed cautious interest; nothing signed.
items.raised_event: Llewellyn's time-crystal offer to Dagmar

items.title: The three magically-sealed chests from the Hound of Cassel raid are still unopened.
items.context: Legal status is a deliberately fuzzy area; the covenant decided to hold them "for now," prepared to return them if Scarem Montem comes asking. Never revisited since.
items.raised_event: Debates about Valerian, new Tribunal, Chests, etc

items.title: The Maelstrom's Maw and Kor Ex Flambeau remain missing.
items.context: Confirmed missing by the GM. The ship never came in and the covenant's Master Chart no longer tracks it; neither Kor nor Nequam (its two former owners) remain part of the active roster. No search or resolution has ever been undertaken.
items.raised_event: The handoff of the Maelstrom's Maw

items.title: Confluensis's public 13th-place humiliation has soured relations, with no repair attempted.
items.context: The "Siege of Shame" — zero pawns, tied to a historical cheating scandal — landed on Confluensis publicly, minutes before Bertrand ex Verditius flatly denied the book-storage arrangement Dagmar and Dustin had negotiated with him. The relationship is currently just... cold.
items.raised_event: Bertrand denies the book-storage arrangement ever happened

items.title: Sjórseiðr's dominant Tribunal win is being read as disruptive — Dietrich named no specifics.
items.context: "I believe they have made some enemies," from someone with no visibility into actual covenant politics, just ambient chatter. A first-place finish over three leash covenants (Confluensis, Montverte, and effectively Fudarus/Oleron's expectations) carries real seven-year resource consequences nobody has mapped out yet.
items.raised_event: Dietrich warns Wilhelm about the company he's keeping

items.title: Scarem Montem's defection to the Lotharingian Tribunal is still rippling, beyond the stolen-thesis entanglement.
items.context: A vassal breaking from its liege (Montverte) at the host's own Tribunal, immediately after stealing the host's prize relic. Sjórseiðr's only current stake in this is Wilhelm's stolen manuscript — the wider political fallout (for Montverte, for the Lotharingian-secession question generally) hasn't touched the covenant directly yet.
items.raised_event: Scarem Montem steals the Tapestry and declares for Lotharingia

items.title: Rán's public appearance at the Tribunal feast is accumulating whispered reputation damage.
items.context: Murmurs of "molesting the fairies" circled the room when Valdemar introduced her openly. A Presence+Guile stress-die success held the appearance for the moment, but nobody has confronted it since — what would actually happen if the Tribunal investigated?
items.raised_event: Valdemar introduces Rán at the feast

items.title: Wilhelm's plan to turn folk magic into a real "pocket" magic system.
items.context: Player's stated research roadmap: (1) mine Hermetic texts — probably a Root or two — for hedge-magic inspiration; (2) turn that into actual Insight, ideally as ceremonial spells folk wizards can learn; (3) send the research assistants out into Ireland to gather more raw material; (4) fold the results back into the folk-magic system properly, which needs formulaic spellcasting (no more halving rolls to cast), ceremonial casting (adding Aura + Philosophiae), and — as a bonus, since folk magic already uses them informally — a correct integration of props. Basic enchanting (already loosely possible via Magic Lore + vis) is flagged as a later, incremental step. Player's own assessment: the first three are "REALLY EASY" to incorporate — the Learned Magicians seem to have worked out parts of it already without any Magic Theory at all.
items.raised_event: Wilhelm pitches Éogan on hedge-magic sea/weather traditions for the thesis

items.title: Wilhelm may pitch the covenant a mundane vis-factory proof-of-concept.
items.context: Once he has his thesis back, Wilhelm's player floated getting the covenant to set up a mundane vis factory if they're short on vis — both a practical fix and a live proof-of-concept for his folk-magic theories.
items.raised_event: Wilhelm's manuscript reveals a Divine-vis wrinkle

items.title: Dietrich plans to self-initiate via Magic Lore so he can formally teach Magic Theory at Cologne.
items.context: Refines the earlier plan (session 7: a season getting initiated into a minor virtue to teach the folk-magic system). Per the player's latest notes, Dietrich is specifically aiming to learn enough Magic Lore to self-initiate — the broader goal being to teach actual Magic Theory at his university, not just the folk system.
items.raised_event: Dietrich pitches folk magic to scholars and a Redcap; Dustin interrogates him

items.title: How does learning a NEW folk-magic guideline work once you're already initiated into a branch?
items.context: Fairly settled: folk magic can be learned via Original Research/Experimentation, or via initiation. Genuinely open: once initiated into a branch (e.g. abjuration, scrying, cursing, warding), does learning a further new guideline in that SAME branch require a full initiation script / Original Research again, or is it progressively easier — the way learning a new scrying guideline gets easier once you're already initiated into scrying generally? Player's stated preference is the latter.
items.raised_event: Dietrich pitches folk magic to scholars and a Redcap; Dustin interrogates him
